prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering hours; safety/headway/dwell/recovery objectives. Line Traffic Controller regulates/authorizes/coordin­ates recovery; Revenue Train Operator owns readiness/procedures/compliance. Voice Dispatch Console supports degraded voice coordination, separate from vital data.
Metro Operations Control System (Lantern) supplies positions/regulation/alarms/commands; sends Crew Login Token Bundle. Service Timetable Server supplies schedule context to Lantern/non-vital functions; enforcement uses safety authority/train state. Passenger Information Gateway distributes approved messages, receives non-vital positions/service states; cannot influence safety.
North District Zone Controller/South District Zone Controller compute authorities from location reports/occupancy/field states. East Junction Interlocking/West Junction Interlocking control vital points/signals; accept only safety-compliant commands; send onboard safety indications.
Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel) requires authentication/energization/valid integrity; supervises protection/authorities/speed/doors/vehicle commands. Modes: initialization, protected manual operation, automatic train operation, fallback operation, cutout. Checks authority sequence/applicability/consistency; recalculates braking each enforcement cycle; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log after enforcement-data validation.
Dual Channel Odometer supplies independent speed/distance; continuous comparison, threshold divergence degrades mode. Reduced confidence increases uncertainty/requests separation-preserving actions. Vehicle interface converts propulsion/braking safety commands with non-vital electrical isolation. Brake assurance checks feedback/pressure/deceleration. Operator interface displays authority/speed/confidence/radio/actions; monitored acknowledgements reach Atlas, rejecting stale/inconsistent commands.
Train Radio Modem maintains sessions over Wayside Radio Access Network; radio subsystem reports quality/registration/continuity to Atlas. Safety Data Communication Network provides segregated, availability-monitored, authenticated/integrity-protected bounded-latency transport; sends Clock Drift Sample Report periodically.
Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges enable/closed-and-locked indications with correctly-berthed train interface.
Signal Maintenance Engineer (Maple) uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server (Quarry), collecting non-vital trainborne health without direct vital access/authority bypass. Cyber Security Officer oversees access/keys/security response via Cryptographic Key Management Appliance; communications security material cannot alter onboard safety logic.
Normal: automatic regulation. Degraded: rulebook-safe state/reduced automation/human confirmation/conservative movement; confidence/communications loss or vital disagreement restricts movement pending resolution/approved procedure.

Document units:
S051: Wayside communications for Greenvale Metro are organized around continuous train radio coverage and a separated safety data backbone that carries vital movement authority traffic.
S052: The Wayside Radio Access Network is sometimes called Saffron in radio survey records, but this document uses Wayside Radio Access Network as the canonical name.
S053: The Wayside Radio Access Network provides overlapping cell coverage through stations, tunnels, crossovers, and depot approach tracks so that the Train Radio Modem can maintain a stable session during normal operation.
S054: Radio sites are engineered with sector overlap at station throats and interlocking approaches because these locations combine frequent braking, switching, and train-to-wayside message activity.
S055: The Train Radio Modem maintains the active bearer used by the Atlas Onboard Controller and reports radio quality changes before the session reaches the minimum design margin.
S056: Handover is planned as a make-before-break event where practical, with the old radio path retained until the new path has accepted the session and passed basic message checks.
S057: If radio quality degrades faster than predicted, the onboard equipment falls back to the last validated movement authority rules rather than accepting unverified wayside data.
S058: The Safety Data Communication Network carries vital messages between zone controllers, interlockings, and approved interfaces using deterministic routing and monitored latency limits.
S059: The Safety Data Communication Network is physically and logically separated from maintenance and passenger information traffic to reduce exposure to congestion and non-vital configuration changes.
S060: Cryptographic Key Management Appliance supports the authentication framework used on the safety data paths and is managed under controlled access by authorized technical staff.
S061: North District Zone Controller is sometimes called Marble in legacy boundary diagrams, but this document uses North District Zone Controller as the canonical name.
S062: South District Zone Controller is sometimes called Orchid in commissioning notes, but this document uses South District Zone Controller as the canonical name.
S063: North District Zone Controller supervises the northern main line, the northern turnback, and the approach to East Junction Interlocking within its configured limits.
S064: South District Zone Controller supervises the southern main line, the southern turnback, and the approach to West Junction Interlocking within its configured limits.
S065: The boundary between North District Zone Controller and South District Zone Controller is defined by track section ownership, radio coverage overlap, and the point at which a train authority must be reissued by the receiving zone.
